name: Extreme heat
value: Severe heatwave, Cape York and Gulf (13 Nov)
summary: BoM severe heatwave warning for Queensland's Peninsula and Gulf Country on 13 Nov; no deadly top-tier event found
state: The Bureau of Meteorology's Queensland warning issued at 1:10pm on 13 Nov covers a severe heatwave in the Gulf Country and Peninsula, with maximums in the high 30s to low 40s°C and overnight lows in the mid to high 20s; it peaks over the Gulf Country and continues on the Peninsula (WillyWeather, citing BoM). It follows an early-November heatwave across northern Australia, with 45.1°C at Fitzroy Crossing on 3 Nov (IQAir). Regional warnings meet the Watch line; no deadly heatwave under top-tier warnings across a large population was found as of 14 Nov.
for_you: Most exposed are remote communities in Cape York and the Gulf Country, older people, young children and outdoor workers. Travellers to northern Australia can follow Bureau of Meteorology warnings and Queensland Health heat advice.
rubric_hit: Severe heatwave warning across Queensland's Peninsula and Gulf: Watch line (regional warnings); no deadly top-tier event

why: Heat is the deadliest weather hazard globally, straining power grids, crops and health systems.
drivers: Heat domes, climate warming, season, humidity, urban heat islands.

rubric.alert: Deadly heatwave with top-tier official warnings across a large population.
rubric.watch: Heatwave warnings across a major region, or national temperature records.
rubric.normal: No major heatwaves affecting large populations.
